questions.problem:
| $x$ | **$-5$** | **$0$** | **$5$** | **$10$** | **$15$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $15$ | $10$ | $5$ | $0$ | $-5$ |

The vector of coefficients  of the line $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above can be found using linear regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?
questions.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$-5$** | **$0$** | **$5$** | **$10$** | **$15$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $15$ | $10$ | $5$ | $0$ | $-5$ |

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 10 \\ 1 & 15\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 10 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

questions.problem:
| $x$ | **$-2$** | **$-1$** | **$0$** | **$1$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $1$ | $5$ | $8$ | $10$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}24 \\ 3\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
questions.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 8 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation 

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}24 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7.5 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $y=7.5+3x.$

questions.problem:
A statistician collected data on the height above the ground (in hundreds of meters) of a hot air balloon during the first five minutes of its flight. This data is shown below. 

| Time $(x)$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Height $(y)$ | $1.6$ | $3.0$ | $4.6$ | $6$ | $7.6$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the balloon's height after $6$ minutes, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}22.8 \\ 83.4\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
questions.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1.6 \\ 3.0 \\ 4.6 \\ 6 \\ 7.6\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}22.8 \\ 83.4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.06 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=0.06+1.5x.$

Finally, to predict the height of the balloon after $6$ minutes, we substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =0.06+1.5(6) \\  & =9.06\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the balloon's height after $6$ minutes will be $906$ meters.  

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=6$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

 

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}31.5 & -11 \\ -11 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}58 \\ 168\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4.2 \\ 6.8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=-4.2+6.8x.$ 

Finally, to predict the value of the sales when the advertising budget is equal to $$5$ million, we substitute $x=5$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-4.2+6.8(5) \\  & =29.8\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the total sales when the advertising budget equals $$5$ million will be $$29.8$ million. 

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=5$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the tree's height after $8$ years, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}15 & -5 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}11.8 \\ 35\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1.2 \\ 2.5 \\ 3.6 \\ 4.5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}15 & -5 \\ -5 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}11.8 \\ 35\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.2 \\ 1.1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=0.2+1.1x.$

Finally, to predict the  height after $8$ years, we substitute $x=8$ into the equation of the line: 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =0.2+1.1(8) \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

 

So, according to the model, the height of a pine tree that is $8$ years old will be $9$ feet. 

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=8$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.
